text: Setting clear project goals is essential for success, and using the SMART framework is a great way to start. SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying "improve the website," a SMART goal would be "increase user sign-ups by 20% within three months." Once your goals are defined, break them into smaller milestones. These are checkpoints that help you track progress and stay motivated. Each milestone should lead to a specific deliverable, such as a report, a prototype, or a completed task. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment by discussing these goals with everyone involved. This way, all team members and clients share the same vision, reducing confusion and improving collaboration.
